teach.heading: TradingView is your workspace, not just a pretty chart.
teach.body: You are using it to read price, change perspective with timeframes, and mark behavior so your eyes stop feeling lost. A horizontal level marking a repeated reaction area is one of the cleanest beginner tools — you don't need every feature, just a few used clearly.
teach.dayliNote: You do not need every feature. A few tools used clearly is better than a messy chart.

experience.intro: Same workspace, tested against a few habits.

steps.prompt: You want to mark a level price keeps reacting to. Which tool fits best?

options.label: A single horizontal level
options.feedback: Right — one clean level beats a cluttered chart every time.

options.label: Every drawing tool at once
options.feedback: Piling on tools usually makes the chart harder to read, not easier.

steps.prompt: Your chart now has 12 different lines, boxes, and indicators layered on top of price. What's the actual effect on your read?

options.label: It gets harder to see what price is actually doing
options.feedback: Exactly — clutter competes with price for your attention.

options.label: It gets easier — more markings means more information
options.feedback: More markings isn't automatically more useful information — often it's just noise.

steps.prompt: You switch from the 4H to the 1M chart. What actually changed?

options.label: Your zoomed-in view of the same market — not the market itself
options.feedback: Right — timeframe changes your perspective, not the underlying price story.

options.label: You're now looking at a completely different market
options.feedback: It's still the same instrument and the same price — just a different zoom level.

reinforce.question: A new trader adds ten different drawing tools to her chart at once, hoping more markings will make her read clearer. What's the better approach, and why?
options: A few tools used clearly — an overloaded chart makes price harder to read, not easier
More tools always means a better read
It doesn't matter how many tools she uses

reinforce.question: A trader believes that adding more drawing tools to her chart will automatically make her analysis more accurate. Is that true? Explain.
reinforce.modelAnswer: No — more tools doesn't mean more accuracy. A cluttered chart makes it harder to see what price is actually doing. A few clearly-used tools (like one clean horizontal level) usually produce a clearer read than a chart covered in every available drawing tool.

reinforce.question: Switching timeframes changes your ___ on the same market, not the market itself.
